newsitem.title: USA: Livingston remains U.S. House Appropriations head.
newsitem.headline: Livingston remains U.S. House Appropriations head.

text.p: Louisiana Republican Rep. Bob Livingston was selected Friday to continue as chairman of the powerful House Appropriations Committee, vowing to push on with his fight to reduce the size of government.

During the past two years as chairman, Livingston has been at the forefront of Republican efforts to balance the budget. The committee sets annual spending levels for federal programs, with the exception of mandatory entitlements.

"My panel's mission, as it has been for the last two years, is to eliminate ineffective government programs and to make sure discretionary spending meets targets for balancing the budget," he said in a statement.

Livingston fended off a challenge from Pennsylvania Republican Rep. Joseph McDade. McDade has more seniority on the committee but was passed over as chairman two years ago because he faced bribery and racketeering charges.

McDade was acquitted in August and pushed House Republican leaders to name him chairman. Feeling that Livingston had performed well in tough budget battles with the White House, the leadership stuck with him.
As a consolation prize, Republican leaders gave McDade the title of commitee vice chairman. He will also become chairman of the subcommittee on energy and water development.
